title: Two tools I left out of NoByte on purpose
summary: A speed test and a currency converter would have been the two most visited pages on the site. Both would have lied to the person using them, so I built neither.

title: The Lights Out hint that was legal but never the smart move
summary: My solver cleared the board, so I called it done. But a solved board has sixteen answers, and it kept handing back a longer one than it needed to.

title: The QR export that came back blank, but only on an iPhone
summary: It rendered on my laptop and downloaded a blank square on a phone. The canvas was not too big for the device, it was too big for one silent limit.

title: The cache-busting hash that had to chase its own tail
summary: I stamped every file with a hash of its bytes, then shipped a change nobody saw. A file's hash does not move when something it imports does.

title: My anti-hallucination filter was deleting the real gaps
summary: It only kept what it could find in the job description. That was right, and it was also throwing away the answers worth reading.

title: The check-then-act race that was charging users twice
summary: It passed every test I wrote, because every test I wrote ran one request at a time.

title: My cache key was wrong, so I billed people for work I had already done
summary: Same job, same resume, second charge. The key was hashing the rendering along with the inputs.

title: What do you rate-limit on? The bug hiding inside "per user"
summary: It said per user. It was keyed on the token, and the client could mint a fresh token whenever it liked.
